correctness.rationale: Reassessed /workspace/repairs/4/RESULT.md. The frozen coefficient statement needed to exclude the constant term: a_0=0 and a_1=L>0 even on the one-vertex tree. The repaired text states the tail formula and monotonicity for j>=1, with the separate constant term. Complements of closed sets are exactly omissions in which each omitted nonleaf has an omitted child. Starting at any omitted u produces a downward path to a leaf; conversely every such path is a minimal omission containing u, since its consecutive children are forced. Proper meet-irreducibles in a finite closure system are precisely maximal closed sets omitting a point: maximal omission implies irreducibility by intersection, and a proper irreducible has a unique cover whose added points occur in every strict superset. Thus distinct ancestor-leaf paths give all proper meet-irreducibles without duplicates. Each leaf supplies exactly one path of each positive size through depth+1; coefficient differences recover the depth histogram. Counting by starting vertex gives at least one path from every vertex, strictly more from any branching vertex. At fixed n and L every leaf depth is at most n-L, and simultaneous equality forces every internal vertex onto every root-to-leaf path, exactly a broom. Each feasible fixed-(n,L) broom exists; the integer quadratic L*(n-L+1) then gives the stated global maximum, including the constrained n=2 case. For n=1 the empty set is the only proper meet-irreducible. The frozen checker and record were read, not executed; they are finite corroboration and unnecessary for this proof.
residual_risks: Only one conjunctive premise per internal vertex in a rooted tree is covered; neither extra rules nor general dependency DAGs have the same argument.

evidence: Babin gives the general maximal-omitter characterization. Defrain et al. express attached irreducibles using transversals of the premises concluding the omitted vertex. Here the unique premise has singleton-child minimal transversals.

Nourine–Vilmin Theorem 5 is an exact acyclic-split recurrence. Deepest leaves form a Boolean factor; maximal lifts of a pruned-tree path complement either keep the omitted path or extend it by one missing child of a newly exposed leaf.
broader_coverage.reasoning: These are materially stronger statements for classification and enumeration. In particular the split recurrence supplies the path description, and path lengths immediately supply the deficit polynomial. Neither recurrence by itself compares model counts across all tree shapes and optimizes them at fixed total vertex number.

evidence: Peeling deepest leaves in the exact split theorem generates the classified paths and thereby the polynomial; that dependence is stated in the repair.

originality.rationale: The repaired Finding is the sharp fixed-total-size (and fixed-leaf-count) model-count bound and its equality cases. The original structural emphasis did not give sufficient credit to concrete implications of earlier, broader Horn results. Acyclic splitting by deepest leaves yields the path complements by induction, and the deficit polynomial is then their length count. The repair explicitly treats both as structural input and corollaries, not the unsupported novelty claim. The checked Horn results do not optimize over rooted trees of a specified total size; Fischer's Sackin extremum fixes leaf count and excludes nonroot unary internal vertices. In the checked sources the extremal model-count remainder is not covered.
residual_risks: The broader Horn coverage is established by specialization, independent of priority claims about the exact wording. The sharp fixed-vertex extremum is assessed on bounded evidence; an uninspected statement for unary-allowed trees with fixed total vertices could cover its tree-statistic formulation. No within-day ordering is inferred from catalogue dates.

value.rationale: The repaired extremum gives the exact worst-case cardinality of the characteristic representation for a canonical acyclic Horn family, including the shapes that blow up the number of models from linear to quadratic. Knowing that an enumeration algorithm is efficient does not give this output bound or identify the maximizing inputs. The fixed-leaf count bound identifies the structural cause of the output growth. The earlier structural specialization and spectrum are useful context but are not counted as additional novel contributions.
residual_risks: The proof is short and tree-specific; no general bound on acyclic Horn output sizes follows from it.
